# PowerShell counters (.ps1, .psm1), for a rule with the prompt file-body-fallback: one per line,
# label TAB pattern (Java regex), keywords in any case as PowerShell reads them. "requirements" is
# [raw]: #Requires is a comment to the parser. The [ignore] line then blanks, leftmost region first,
# block comments (<# ... #>), here-strings (@" or @' at the end of a line up to "@ or '@ first on a
# line), # comments and string literals, so a "function" in a help comment or a string does not
# count. A string may span lines, as PowerShell reads it; a block comment, a here-string or a string
# that is never closed runs to the end of the file.
# "mandatory parameters" counts Mandatory and Mandatory = $true, not Mandatory = $false; "dot-sourced
# scripts" a line starting with ". " and a path, a quoted one too (the blanked string leaves the
# ". " and nothing or the arguments after it). "Verb-Noun command calls (approx)" counts every name of
# the Verb-Noun shape in any case, as PowerShell resolves a command (ForEach-Object, ConvertTo-Json,
# get-childitem), a call of the script's own functions too, but not the name a function, filter or
# workflow defines; a hyphenated word outside a string (a host name argument) counts too. OpsFactPatternsTest pins
# every case; ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that every pattern reads linearly.
[raw] requirements
[ignore] comments, here-strings and strings
functions
advanced functions
parameter blocks
mandatory parameters
classes
modules imported
dot-sourced scripts
try blocks
errors raised
